title: Chapter 2: Atoms, Molecules, and Ions

2.4 Ionic and Molecular Compounds

In ordinary chemical reactions, the nucleus of each atom (and thus the identity of the element) remains unchanged. Electrons, however, can be added to atoms by transfer from other atoms, lost by transfer to other atoms, or shared with other atoms. The transfer and sharing of electrons govern the chemistry of elements. During the formation of compounds, atoms gain or lose electrons to form electrically charged particles called ions.

  • Cation: A positively charged ion formed when a neutral atom loses one or more electrons. For example, a neutral sodium atom (Na, 11 protons, 11 electrons) loses 1 electron to form Na⁺ (11 protons, 10 electrons). The cation's electron cloud is smaller than that of the neutral atom.
  • Anion: A negatively charged ion formed when a neutral atom gains one or more electrons. For example, a neutral bromine atom (Br, 35 protons, 35 electrons) gains 1 electron to form Br⁻ (35 protons, 36 electrons).

Predicting Ion Charges from the Periodic Table

Main-group elements typically gain or lose electrons to achieve the electron configuration of the nearest noble gas:

  • Group 1 (Alkali Metals): Lose 1 electron → 1+ charge (e.g., Li⁺, Na⁺, K⁺, Ca²⁺ lost 2 e⁻).
  • Group 2 (Alkaline Earth Metals): Lose 2 electrons → 2+ charge (e.g., Mg²⁺, Ca²⁺, Ba²⁺).
  • Group 15 (Pnictogens): Gain 3 electrons → 3- charge (e.g., N³⁻, P³⁻).
  • Group 16 (Chalcogens): Gain 2 electrons → 2- charge (e.g., O²⁻, S²⁻, Se²⁻).
  • Group 17 (Halogens): Gain 1 electron → 1- charge (e.g., F⁻, Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻).
  • Transition Metals: Often exhibit variable charges that cannot be predicted solely by group position (e.g., Cu⁺/Cu²⁺, Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺, Cr³⁺/Cr⁶⁺).

👉 በተለመዱ የኬሚካል ሪአክሽኖች ጊዜ የአተሙ ኒዩክለስ (የፕሮቶን ቁጥር) አይቀየርም። ነገር ግን ኤሌክትሮኖች ሲሰጡ፣ ሲወሰዱ ወይም ሲጋሩ አዮኖች (Ions) ይፈጠራሉ። አተሞች ኤሌክትሮን ሲያጡ ፖዘቲቭ ቻርጅ ያለው Cation (መጠናቸው ከአተሙ ያነሰ)፣ ኤሌክትሮን ሲቀበሉ ደግሞ ኔገቲቭ ቻርጅ ያለው Anion ይፈጠራሉ። የፔሪዮዲክ ሰንጠረዥን በመጠቀም የአንድን አተም አዮኒክ ቻርጅ በቀላሉ መገመት እንችላለን፤ ግሩፕ 1 ሁልጊዜ +1፣ ግሩፕ 2 ደግሞ +2 አዮን ሲፈጥሩ፤ ግሩፕ 17 ደግሞ -1፣ ግሩፕ 16 -2 ቻርጅ ያመጣሉ። Transition metals ደግሞ ተለዋዋጭ ቻርጅ አላቸው።

Worked Examples & Practice Exercises

Example 2.5: Naming Groups of Elements
Give the group name for: (a) Chlorine, (b) Calcium, (c) Sodium.
Solution:
(a) Chlorine (Group 17) = Halogen
(b) Calcium (Group 2) = Alkaline earth metal
(c) Sodium (Group 1) = Alkali metal

Check Your Learning (Example 2.5):
Give the group name for: (a) Krypton, (b) Selenium, (c) Lithium, (d) Barium.
Solution: (a) Noble gas, (b) Chalcogen (Group 16), (c) Alkali metal, (d) Alkaline earth metal.

Example 2.6: Composition of Ions
An ion found in antiperspirants contains 13 protons and 10 electrons. What is its symbol?
Solution:
1. Protons = 13 → Atomic number 13 corresponds to Aluminum (Al).
2. Charge = Protons - Electrons = 13 - 10 = +3.
3. Symbol = Al³⁺ (Aluminum cation).

Example 2.7: Formation of Ions
Magnesium and nitrogen react to form an ionic compound. Predict which forms an anion, which forms a cation, and the charges of each ion. Write the symbol and name for each ion.
Solution:
1. Magnesium (Group 2, metal) loses 2 e⁻ → Cation: Mg²⁺ (magnesium ion).
2. Nitrogen (Group 15, nonmetal) gains 3 e⁻ → Anion: N³⁻ (nitride ion).

Check Your Learning (Example 2.7):
1. Give the symbol and name for the ion with 34 protons and 36 electrons.
Solution: Atomic number 34 = Selenium (Se). Charge = 34 - 36 = -2. Symbol: Se²⁻ (Selenide ion).
2. Aluminum and carbon react to form an ionic compound. Predict cation, anion, charges, symbols, and names.
Solution: Aluminum loses 3 e⁻ → Al³⁺ (aluminum ion, cation). Carbon gains 4 e⁻ → C⁴⁻ (carbide ion, anion).

Monatomic vs Polyatomic Ions and Oxyanions

Ions formed from only one atom are monatomic ions (e.g., Na⁺, Cl⁻). Polyatomic ions are electrically charged molecules consisting of a group of bonded atoms with an overall charge (e.g., NH₄⁺, SO₄²⁻).

Oxyanions are polyatomic ions containing one or more oxygen atoms. Nomenclature rules for oxyanions:

  • -ate suffix: Used for the oxyanion with more oxygen atoms (e.g., Nitrate NO₃⁻, Sulfate SO₄²⁻).
  • -ite suffix: Used for the oxyanion with fewer oxygen atoms (e.g., Nitrite NO₂⁻, Sulfite SO₃²⁻).
  • per- prefix + -ate: State with the maximum oxygen atoms (e.g., Perchlorate ClO₄⁻).
  • hypo- prefix + -ite: State with the minimum oxygen atoms (e.g., Hypochlorite ClO⁻).

👉 አዮኖች ከአንድ አተም ብቻ ከተሰሩ Monatomic ይባላሉ (እንደ Na⁺, Cl⁻)። ከአንድ በላይ አተሞች ተጣብቀው የጋራ ቻርጅ ካላቸው ደግሞ Polyatomic ions ይባላሉ (እንደ SO₄²⁻, NH₄⁺)። ኦክሲጅን የያዙ ፖሊአቶሚክ አዮኖች Oxyanions ይባላሉ። ስያሜአቸውም በኦክሲጅን ብዛት ይወሰናል፦ በበዛው ላይ '-ate' (ለምሳሌ Nitrate NO₃⁻)፣ ባነሰው ላይ '-ite' (Nitrite NO₂⁻) እንጨምራለን። በጣም ከበዛ 'per-'፣ በጣም ካነሰ ደግሞ 'hypo-' ቅጥያዎችን እንጠቀማለን (ለምሳሌ ClO₄⁻ Perchlorate ሲሆን ClO⁻ ደግሞ Hypochlorite ነው)።

2.4.1 Formation of Ionic Compounds

When an element composed of atoms that readily lose electrons (a metal) reacts with an element that readily gains electrons (a nonmetal), a transfer of electrons occurs, producing ions. The resulting compound is held together by ionic bonds, which are electrostatic forces of attraction between ions of opposite charge.

  • Electrical Neutrality: Every ionic compound must be electrically neutral overall. The total positive charge of the cations must equal the total negative charge of the anions.
  • Physical Properties: Ionic compounds are crystalline solids with high melting and boiling points (e.g., NaCl melts at 801 °C and boils at 1413 °C).
  • Electrical Conductivity: In solid state, ionic compounds do NOT conduct electricity because ions cannot move freely. When molten (liquid) or dissolved in water (aqueous), they conduct electricity because ions move freely.
  • Polyatomic Ionic Compounds: Polyatomic ions act as discrete units. Parentheses are used when more than one polyatomic ion is present in the formula (e.g., Ca₃(PO4)₂).
  • Empirical Formula Exception: While ionic formulas represent empirical formulas (lowest whole-number ratio), discrete polyatomic ions retain their formula (e.g., Sodium oxalate is written as Na₂C₂O₄, NOT NaCO₂, because C₂O₄²⁻ is a single polyatomic anion).

👉 አዮኒክ ኮምፓውንድ የሚፈጠረው በብረት (Metal) እና በብረት ያልሆነ (Non-metal) አተሞች መካከል ኤሌክትሮን ሙሉ ለሙሉ ሲተላለፍ ነው። በአንዮን እና በካቲዮን መካከል ያለው የኤሌክትሮስታቲክ ሳብ ionic bond ይባላል። አዮኒክ ኮምፓውንዶች ሁልጊዜ በቻርጅ Neutral መሆን አለባቸው። በSolid ደረጃ ኤሌክትሪክ አያስተላልፉም (አዮኖቹ ስለማይንቀሳቀሱ)፤ ነገር ግን ሲቀልጡ (Molten) ወይም በውሃ ሲበላሹ ኤሌክትሪክ ያስተላልፋሉ። ፖሊአቶሚክ አዮን ከ1 በላይ ካስፈልገን በቅንፍ (parentheses) ውስጥ አድርገን ታች subscript እንጽፋለን (ለምሳሌ Ca₃(PO₄)₂)።

💡 Exam Hint:
ፈተና ላይ ሊያሳስቱ የሚችሉ ወሳኝ ነጥቦች ፦
1. AlCl₃ በብረት እና በኖን-ሜታል የተሰራ ቢሆንም አዮኒክ አይደለም (Covalent character አለው)!
2. Sodium Oxalate ፎርሙላ Na₂C₂O₄ ነው እንጂ ተቃጥሎ NaCO₂ አይባልም! ምክንያቱም C₂O₄²⁻ የተባለው ፖሊአቶሚክ አዮን አይነጣጠልም።
3. Solid ionic compounds ኤሌክትሪክ አያስተላልፉም፤ ኤሌክትሪክ የሚያስተላልፉት Molten (ሲቀልጡ) ወይም Aqueous (በውሃ ሲሟሙ) ብቻ ነው!

Example 2.8: Predicting the Formula of an Ionic Compound
The gemstone sapphire is mostly a compound of aluminum and oxygen containing Al³⁺ and O²⁻ ions. What is its formula?
Solution:
1. Charges must balance: Cation charge (+3), Anion charge (-2).
2. Least common multiple of 3 and 2 is 6.
3. Two Al³⁺ ions give 2 × (+3) = +6.
4. Three O²⁻ ions give 3 × (-2) = -6.
5. Formula = Al₂O₃.

Example 2.9: Compound with a Polyatomic Anion
Baking powder contains calcium dihydrogen phosphate, composed of Ca²⁺ and H₂PO₄⁻ ions. What is the formula?
Solution:
1. Calcium charge = 2+.
2. Dihydrogen phosphate charge = 1-.
3. Need two H₂PO₄⁻ ions to balance one Ca²⁺ ion.
4. Formula = Ca(H₂PO₄)₂.

Check Your Learning (Section 2.4.1):
1. Predict the formula formed between lithium ion (Li⁺) and peroxide ion (O₂²⁻).
Solution: 2 Li⁺ (+2 total) balances 1 O₂²⁻ (-2 total) → Li₂O₂.
2. Predict the formula formed between sodium cation (Na⁺) and sulfide anion (S²⁻).
Solution: 2 Na⁺ (+2 total) balances 1 S²⁻ (-2 total) → Na₂S.

2.4.2 Formation of Molecular Compounds

Many compounds do not contain ions but consist solely of discrete, neutral molecules. Molecular compounds (covalent compounds) result when atoms share rather than transfer electrons. Covalent bonds are attractive forces between the positively charged nuclei of bonded atoms and shared electron pairs.

  • Composition: Formed usually by a combination of nonmetals (e.g., H₂O, CO₂, NH₃).
  • Physical Properties: Under normal conditions, molecular compounds often exist as gases, low-boiling liquids, and low-melting solids.
  • Predicting Bond Types:
    - Metal + Nonmetal → Ionic (usually)
    - Nonmetal + Nonmetal → Molecular / Covalent
    - Contains Polyatomic Ion → Ionic

👉 Covalent (Molecular) compounds የሚፈጠሩት ሁለት ወይም ከዚያ በላይ የሆኑ Nonmetals ኤሌክትሮኖችን እኩል ሲጋሩ ነው። አዮን አይፈጥሩም። እነዚህ ኮምፓውንዶች አነስተኛ የመቅለጫ እና የመፍላት ነጥብ ስላላቸው በተፈጥሮ ጋዝ፣ ዝቅተኛ የመፍላት ነጥብ ያላቸው ፈሳሾች ወይም ለስላሳ ሶሊዶች ናቸው።

Example 2.10: Predicting the Type of Bonding in Compounds
Predict whether the following compounds are ionic or molecular:
(a) KI (table salt iodine source)
(b) H₂O₂ (bleach and disinfectant hydrogen peroxide)
(c) CHCl₃ (anesthetic chloroform)
(d) Li₂CO₃ (source of lithium in antidepressants)
Solution:
(a) KI: Potassium (Group 1 metal) + Iodine (Group 17 nonmetal) → Ionic.
(b) H₂O₂: Hydrogen (nonmetal) + Oxygen (nonmetal) → Molecular.
(c) CHCl₃: Carbon (nonmetal) + Hydrogen (nonmetal) + Chlorine (nonmetal) → Molecular.
(d) Li₂CO₃: Lithium (Group 1 metal) + Carbonate (polyatomic anion) → Ionic.
